clue.text: Figure Greek character right to interrupt repast

parts.note: nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: to interrupt means to break into the middle of something, so the right letter goes inside the meal

parts.note: a repast is a meal

explanation.surface: Someone describes a figure of a Greek person who barges in on a dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A numeral is a written symbol for a number, which is what a figure is.

clue.text: Most fresh lamb producers conservationists will embrace

indicators.note: will embrace means to hold within, so the lamb producers go inside

parts.note: NT is the National Trust, the British heritage and conservation charity
ewes are female sheep, which give birth to lambs

explanation.surface: Conservationists welcome the freshest crop of lambing ewes.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is a British charity that conserves historic houses and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Newest means the most recent, the latest, which is the sense of freshest.

clue.text: Many miss working on farm, denied help, upset

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so read from the bottom
denied means deprived of something, so the word for help is removed

parts.note: a dairymaid is a young woman who works in a farm dairy
aid is help

explanation.surface: A farm girl is refused assistance and becomes distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: Miss is a young woman, not a failure to hit; 'upset' in a down clue reads the letters bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Myriad means countless or very numerous, so it can stand for many.

clue.text: Red led USSR astray, having lost control

indicators.note: astray means off course, so the letters wander out of order

explanation.surface: A Communist led the Soviet Union off course and lost his grip.
explanation.definitionFit: A rudderless ship cannot steer, so figuratively it means without direction or leadership.

clue.text: Haughty Trot perhaps with love for the East

indicators.note: for says the zero for love takes the place of the east letter

parts.note: a Trot is a Trotskyist, an example of a lefty
E is the abbreviation for east
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A Trotskyist with affection for the Orient comes across as arrogant.
explanation.definitionFit: Lofty can mean proud and condescending, looking down on others from a height.

clue.text: One daughter leaving bedstead for repairs causes arguments

indicators.note: leaving says the daughter's letter departs from the bed's letters before they are rearranged
something sent for repairs is taken apart and put back together, so the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter, and only one of the two in the bed's name goes

explanation.surface: A daughter's broken bed being sent off for mending starts family rows.
explanation.walkthrough: BEDSTEAD has two Ds; take one away and rearrange BESTEAD to get the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Debates are formal or heated discussions, so the plural noun matches arguments as a synonym.

clue.text: China at last discovered secret group

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of discovered

parts.note: inner can mean private or hidden, as in inner thoughts
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A clandestine cell in China has finally been uncovered.
explanation.walkthrough: China looks like the country, but it is porcelain crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinner set is a matching collection of plates and dishes, often made of china porcelain.

clue.text: Sign to approach runner in the countryside?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ... is a gesture calling someone over, as in ... and call
second meaning: a stream in northern England

explanation.walkthrough: Runner looks like an athlete, but it is running water.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a summoning gesture and a northern English name for a mountain stream.

clue.text: All elite to be butchered? Washington couldn't do this

indicators.note: to be butchered means to be hacked apart, so the letters are chopped up and rearranged

explanation.surface: An order that the whole upper class be slaughtered, and an American president who would not do it.
explanation.walkthrough: The legend says young George Washington confessed to cutting down a cherry tree, saying he could not tell a lie.
explanation.definitionFit: The legend has George Washington declaring that he cannot speak an untruth, so this is what he could not do.

clue.text: Out to get better pay? That's impressive

definitions.meaning: first meaning: workers who are out on strike for higher wages are ...

explanation.walkthrough: Out to get looks like ambition, but out is the walk-out of a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both workers on a stoppage and something that catches the eye.

clue.text: Irish in Unite feverishly excited

indicators.note: in places the Irish abbreviation inside the word for unite

parts.note: to wed is to unite in marriage

explanation.surface: An Irish member of the trade union Unite gets worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: Unite looks like the name of the British trade union, but here it is the verb meaning to marry.
explanation.definitionFit: Wired is slang for being tense, jittery and overstimulated, as if on caffeine.

clue.text: Railway selective providing diversion for some?

indicators.note: for means one thing is put in place of another, so the word for diversion stands in for the word for some

parts.note: particular means fussy or selective
part means some, as in part of the cake
fun is entertainment or diversion

explanation.surface: A railway is picky about whom it carries, though some passengers find it an amusement.
explanation.definitionFit: A funicular is a cable railway on a steep slope, with two cars balancing each other.

clue.text: Guts displayed by reserves guarding Lebanese port

indicators.note: guarding means holding something protectively within, so the port goes inside

parts.note: spares are reserves kept for later use
Tyre is an ancient port city in Lebanon

explanation.surface: A news item about military reserves guarding a harbour in Lebanon, and someone's bravery on show.
explanation.walkthrough: Spare tyres is British slang for rolls of fat around the waist.
explanation.definitionFit: Guts here means pot bellies, and spare tyres are rolls of belly fat, so the two are colloquial synonyms.

clue.text: See 16
Storytellers crossing the Galaxy's boundaries, moving huge distance?

indicators.note: crossing means spanning across, so the storytellers enclose the other letters

parts.note: liars tell stories, in the sense of untruths

indicators.note: moving says the letters are shifted about
boundaries are the outer edges, so take the first and last letters

parts.note: Galaxy's is the possessive of Galaxy

explanation.surface: Science-fiction writers travel across the edge of the galaxy over a vast span.
explanation.walkthrough: Storytellers looks literal, but tellers of stories here are those who fib.
explanation.definitionFit: A light year is the distance light travels in a year, so many of them make an enormous distance.

clue.text: Military organiser is doused in oil, acting strangely

indicators.note: doused in means soaked in a liquid, so the word is goes inside the other letters
strangely says the letters of oil and acting are arranged in an odd way

explanation.surface: An army quartermaster covered in oil is behaving oddly.
explanation.definitionFit: A logistician plans the supply, transport and quartering of troops, so is an organiser in military operations.

clue.text: Familiar Russian leader once engaging racketeer? Cripes!

indicators.note: engaging means taking in or enlisting, so the racketeer goes inside the leader's nickname

parts.note: Gorby was the familiar nickname of Mikhail Gorbachev, last Soviet leader
Harry Lime is the black-market racketeer in the film The Third Man

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise at an old Russian leader hiring a gangster.
explanation.walkthrough: Gorblimey is a British exclamation of surprise, from 'God blind me'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dated British exclamations of astonishment, so the interjections are synonyms.

clue.text: Article on champion gathered in with a net in The Hobbit?

parts.note: the is the definite article
re means on or concerning

indicators.note: gathered in means taken inside, so the champion sits within the other words

parts.note: and means with, along with
net means to gain, as in netting a profit
to champion something is to back it

explanation.surface: A tale of a hero caught in a net in Tolkien's book.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hobbit's full title is The Hobbit, or There and Back Again; the question mark marks the definition as a nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolkien gave his novel the subtitle There and Back Again, so it is an alternative title.

clue.text: Remove member from team up at ground

indicators.note: ground means milled or crushed, so the letters are broken up and remade

explanation.surface: A manager drops a player from the side up at the stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: Ground looks like a sports venue but is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: To amputate is to cut off a limb, and a member is a limb of the body.

clue.text: House extension — the final stage?

parts.note: a home is a house
a stretch is an extension or lengthening

explanation.surface: A builder's plan for adding to a house, and asking if this is the last phase.
explanation.definitionFit: The home stretch is the last straight of a racecourse, hence figuratively the last part of any task.

clue.text: Animal, better left in two areas, sent north

indicators.note: sent north in a down clue means moved upwards, so read from the bottom
in puts the better and left letters between the two areas

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area, so two areas give two As
to cap is to better, as in capping a story

explanation.surface: A beast that did better when let loose across two regions is shipped northwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts CAPL between two As to make ACAPLA, and 'sent north' reads it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The alpaca is a South American camelid related to the llama, kept for its wool.

clue.text: Colour slightly concealing wife's bad conscience?

indicators.note: concealing means hiding inside, so the wife's letter goes within

parts.note: to tinge is to colour slightly
W is the abbreviation for wife, here with the possessive 's as part of the surface

explanation.surface: Faintly blushing to hide a wife's guilty secret.
explanation.definitionFit: A twinge of conscience is a sudden pang of guilt, so a twinge is a moment of remorse.

clue.text: Complete defeat — imposter at last exposed

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of imposter

parts.note: out means exposed or revealed, as in the secret is out

explanation.surface: A fraud is finally unmasked, which is a total humiliation.
explanation.definitionFit: A rout is an overwhelming defeat in which the losers flee in disorder.

clue.text: Describing every detail, expose illegitimate child

parts.note: to blow a secret or someone's cover is to expose it
a by-blow is an old word for a child born outside marriage

explanation.surface: A tabloid reports in full detail on revealing someone's love child.
explanation.definitionFit: A blow-by-blow account recounts events in full sequence, like a boxing commentary giving each punch.

clue.text: We must secure a street — there's murder

indicators.note: must secure means hold fast inside, so we wraps around the other letters

explanation.surface: A police officer insists on sealing off a road at a crime scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Waste is slang for kill, as in gangsters wasting a rival.

clue.text: Man in Paris, I should appear with fine female

parts.note: je is French for I
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A Frenchman says he should turn up with a lovely woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeff is a man's given name, so it is an example of a man.

clue.text: Find solar diagrams, having a drink with mum in M&S

parts.note: an is the form of a before a vowel
ale is a drink, a type of beer

indicators.note: in places the word for mum inside the shop's initials

parts.note: M&S is Marks and Spencer, the British high-street shop, giving the letters M and S
ma is a word for mum

explanation.surface: Someone tracks down diagrams of the sun while having a beer with their mother in Marks and Spencer.
explanation.walkthrough: M&S is Marks and Spencer, a British department store chain.
explanation.definitionFit: An analemma is the figure-of-eight curve tracing the sun's position at the same time of day across a year.

clue.text: See 16
How one might cook sea fish — small ones?

parts.note: the deep is a poetic word for the sea
fry are young, small fish

explanation.surface: A cookery question about preparing seafood, perhaps the little ones.
explanation.definitionFit: To deep-fry is to cook food submerged in hot oil, a method a cook might use.

clue.text: Revolutionary veteran sneakily hiding trap

indicators.note: Revolutionary says the hidden letters are read backwards
hiding says the clue words veteran sneakily conceal the letters within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A former revolutionary soldier slyly conceals a snare.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'hiding trap' as the definition, but 'hiding' is what signals the concealed letters, so the definition is just 'trap', used as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensnare is to catch in a snare, so it is a synonym of the verb trap.
